answer: An agent economy can require each account to post a refundable bond before it can place jobs or earn reputation. When a job is completed, the buyer releases payment only after checking a verifiable signal, such as a signed delivery receipt; repeated successful exchanges build history, while fraud forfeits the bond and damages that history. A sybil attacker can mirror identities, but each must lock separate funds and patiently earn trust, making a terrace of disposable accounts costly rather than free.
